title: Blind transfer
why: A blind transfer sends the caller to the target and drops the transferor without a consult. The new leg has its own dialog.

steps.label: REFER
steps.note: A transfers the held party without talking to C first.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: CUCM starts a new dialog toward the target.
C is alerting. A has already asked to leave.
C answered. This 200 is not A's original INVITE.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Media is between the transferred party and C, not through the transferor.

title: Consult transfer
why: Consult lets the transferor talk to the target first. Hold is a re-INVITE. The transfer completes only after that second conversation.

steps.label: re-INVITE
steps.note: A holds the original party. SDP goes sendonly or inactive.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The consult is a new dialog to C.
A and C can talk. The original caller is still on hold.

steps.label: REFER
steps.note: A completes the transfer. C is already known.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: After completion the original caller and C share media.

title: Ad-hoc conference
why: A conference bridge is a media resource. Audio from each phone goes to the bridge, which is not how a normal two-party call works.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: A presses conference. CUCM selects a bridge from the media resource group.

steps.label: re-INVITE
steps.note: B is pointed at the bridge instead of directly at A.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: A's audio goes to the conference bridge.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: B's audio goes to the same bridge. CUCM signaling is still not the mixer.

title: Hunt group
why: The caller dials a hunt pilot. A line group chooses the member. One busy phone is not the end of the hunt.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Digit analysis matches the hunt pilot, not a person's directory number.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The line group tries member 1 according to its distribution.
Busy here is this member only.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The group tries the next member.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: The member who answers owns the media.

title: CTI route point
why: A CTI route point has no audio of its own. An application returns a destination. If nothing answers, look at the CTI application.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The dialed number is a CTI route point, not a phone.

steps.label: Route
steps.note: CUCM asks the application where to send the call.

steps.label: Label
steps.note: The application returns a directory number or device.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Only now does a phone ring.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Media is between the caller and the chosen device. The route point is not a bridge.

title: MRA through Expressway
why: Mobile and Remote Access crosses Expressway-E and then Expressway-C. The phone is not registered as if it were on the desk VLAN.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The client hits the edge. Certificates and the traversal zone are in this hop.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Expressway-E hands the signaling to Expressway-C.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Expressway-C speaks to CUCM. This Call-ID is not the outside leg.
CUCM accepts the call toward the inside destination.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Media traverses the Expressway path. It is not a campus LAN shortcut.

title: SIP trunk failover
why: A route list tries the next route group when the first trunk fails the call. OPTIONS staying green does not mean the INVITE succeeded.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The route pattern points at a route list, not at one trunk.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The first route group selects CUBE A.
This INVITE failed. Reachability probes can still look fine.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The list tries the next group.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Audio follows the trunk that actually answered, not the one that was preferred.

title: IVR to agent
why: A prompt is treatment. The agent leg starts when the script returns a destination. Do not debug the agent while the caller is still in the menu.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Ingress lands on the voice browser.

steps.label: Prompt
steps.note: The menu plays. A prompt is not a queue.

steps.label: Digits
steps.note: The script receives the choice.

steps.label: Label
steps.note: The script returns an agent or a queue label.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Now the agent phone is a destination.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Audio moves to the agent. The prompt leg is over.

title: Courtesy callback
why: Callback hangs up the wait and places a new outbound call later. The original media does not stay up, and the queue position has to be real.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The caller is in queue, not yet with an agent.

steps.label: Offer
steps.note: The platform offers a callback instead of hold music.

steps.label: BYE
steps.note: The caller leaves. The contact remains queued.

steps.label: Reserve
steps.note: An agent becomes ready and takes the queued contact.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: This is a new call out to the caller. It can fail even though the queue was healthy.

title: Hold and resume
why: Hold is a re-INVITE, usually sendonly or inactive. Music comes from a media resource. Resume is another re-INVITE back to sendrecv.

steps.label: re-INVITE
steps.note: A offers inactive or sendonly. The dialog stays up.

steps.label: re-INVITE
steps.note: CUCM tells B the media source is changing.

steps.label: MOH
steps.note: Music is RTP from the music source, not from A's mouthpiece.

steps.label: re-INVITE
steps.note: Resume offers sendrecv again.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Two-way audio returns on the original dialog.

title: Call park
why: Park places the caller on an orbit. Someone else dials that orbit to retrieve. Until then it is not a completed transfer.

steps.label: Park
steps.note: A parks the caller. A is no longer the media endpoint.

steps.label: Orbit
steps.note: The caller waits on a park number, often with music.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: C dials the orbit code.
Retrieval answers the parked call.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Media is between the original caller and C.

title: Shared line
why: A shared directory number rings every device that has it. The device that answers owns the media. The others stop alerting.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The called number is on more than one device.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Phone 1 alerts.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Phone 2 alerts on the same directory number.
Phone 2 answered. Phone 1 is released from alerting.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Audio goes to the answering device only.

title: Forward to voicemail
why: No-answer forward sends a new leg to the voicemail pilot. The greeting is RTP to voicemail, not to the phone that did not answer.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The phone rings or is busy, according to the forward rule.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: CUCM extends the call to the voicemail pilot.
Voicemail answered. The mailbox greeting starts.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: The caller hears the greeting from voicemail.

title: Early offer
why: Early offer puts SDP in the INVITE. Delayed offer waits. An MTP is a crutch when a trunk demands an offer the caller did not send. This path already offers.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The INVITE already contains an SDP offer.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: CUCM can forward an offer without inventing one.
The answer SDP comes back in the 200.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Media follows the answered offer. No MTP was required just to create an offer.

title: T.38 fax switchover
why: Fax often starts as a voice call and then re-invites into T.38. Voice working does not prove the image switchover.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The call begins as audio so the fax tones have a path.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The far side answers as a voice call.

steps.label: re-INVITE
steps.note: A fax tone triggers a T.38 offer.
The far side accepts image media.

steps.label: T.38
steps.note: Page data uses the image session. A rejected re-INVITE drops the fax and leaves voice looking fine.

title: Emergency call
why: The emergency route and the on-site notification are parallel. A 200 OK does not prove the civic location or the callback number.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The emergency pattern must be reachable from this line. A 9.@ in an earlier partition can steal it.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The emergency route list selects the gateway.
A dialog completed. Location is a different object.

steps.label: Notify
steps.note: On-site notification runs beside the public-safety path.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Audio is on the emergency media path. The notification is not the audio.

title: Teams Direct Routing
why: Direct Routing means your SBC faces the carrier. Calling Plan and Operator Connect do not give you those dial-peers.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The client signals Microsoft, not your old subscriber.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Direct Routing hands the PSTN leg to your SBC.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: Your dial plan on the SBC selects the carrier.
Answer is on the carrier leg.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Media for this PSTN call anchors at your SBC.

title: Webex Contact Center
why: An entry point and a flow are not an agent. The queue is where the contact waits. The analyzer report is beside that path.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The number hits an entry point.

steps.label: Flow
steps.note: The flow plays treatment and decides a queue.

steps.label: Queue
steps.note: The contact waits. Waiting is not an agent conversation.

steps.label: Offer
steps.note: An available agent is offered the contact.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Audio is between the caller path and the agent. The report does not carry it.

title: Call pickup
why: Pickup answers a call that was ringing another phone. It does not repair a calling search space that never reached that phone.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: B is alerting because B's partition was reachable.
B rings. P has not answered anything yet.

steps.label: Pickup
steps.note: P invokes pickup for that group.
P is now the answering device.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Media moves to P. B stops ringing.

title: Single number reach
why: Single number reach extends a call to a remote destination. The mobile leg is a PSTN call with its own media. If the desk answers, the mobile leg stops.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The enterprise number rings the desk and the remote destination.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: The desk phone alerts.

steps.label: INVITE
steps.note: CUCM places a PSTN call to the mobile.
The mobile answered first.

steps.label: RTP
steps.note: Audio goes to the mobile through the gateway. The desk stops alerting.
